subproblems.title: Antilipschitz charts pull back Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 we have Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ Z : Set (Eucl P), (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) Z = 0 → (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' Z) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null of DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_area_formula-a1.chart_preimage_null-a1 (status accepted since 2026-10-12T05:20:13Z, candidate commit 9080c178c7e23350ae33476f7bfa68f0965fe15e, isolated comparator passed, no dependencies; already reused by root.deformation-a1.skeleton_polyhedral-a1). Its frozen Lean type, title and statement are copied byte-for-byte from that node, so the runtime maps this key onto the accepted checkpoint by Lean name and provisions no new worker. The proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim; inside it, “the parent” and “the parent proof” mean root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_area_formula-a1, not lpf_chart_chain_rule. Use in lpf_chart_chain_rule: step 1 (Hⁿ-null subsets of ℝ^P pull back to Lⁿ-null parameter sets), consumed by the new child ae_pullback (Submission.lpf_ccr_ae_pullback), steps 0, 1 and 3.

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the estimate of step 1 of the parent proof: Ψ = (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so it maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ(Ω) to Lⁿ-null sets (Lⁿ(Ψ(Z)) ≤ c^{−n} Hⁿ(Z)).

1. Φ is injective on Ω: if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so |w − w′| = 0 since c > 0.
2. If Ω = ∅, then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise ℝⁿ is nonempty and Ψ := Function.invFunOn Φ Ω satisfies Ψ(Φ(w)) = w for all w ∈ Ω (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
3. Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω): for y = Φ(w), y′ = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω, |Ψ(y) − Ψ(y′)| = |w − w′| ≤ c⁻¹|Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| = c⁻¹|y − y′| (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul with constant Real.toNNReal c⁻¹).
4. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)): if w ∈ Ω and Φ(w) ∈ Z then Φ(w) ∈ Z ∩ Φ(Ω) and Ψ(Φ(w)) = w.
5. Lipschitz maps increase Hⁿ by at most the n-th power of the constant (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, scaled by the normalizing factor of μHE[n]; packaged as SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, which is in scope): Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z) = 0.
6. On ℝⁿ, Lⁿ = Hⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By monotonicity and steps 4–5, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = Hⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) ≤ Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz with c > 0 gives injectivity on Ω; Ψ := invFunOn Φ Ω is a left inverse on Ω.
Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω).
Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)).
Hⁿ Lipschitz image bound (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) gives Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0.
Lⁿ = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ concludes.

subproblems.title: Countable open cover with Lipschitz pieces for a map locally Lipschitz on an arbitrary set (parent step 1)
subproblems.statement: For all P, Q ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every map f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q that is locally Lipschitz on U, there are open sets O_i ⊆ ℝ^P and constants K_i ∈ ℝ≥0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i and f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U for every i. Here 'locally Lipschitz on U' means: every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood t within U (t ∈ 𝓝[U] x) and a constant K ≥ 0 such that f is K-Lipschitz on t.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ∃ (O : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (K : ℕ → ℝ≥0), (∀ i, IsOpen (O i)) ∧ U ⊆ ⋃ i, O i ∧ ∀ i, LipschitzOnWith (K i) f (O i ∩ U)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover of DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.locally_lipschitz_image-a1.countable_lipschitz_cover-a1 (status accepted since 2026-10-12T08:47:11Z, candidate commit 6941b70febfeca396a5e8105097428578fe61416, isolated comparator passed, no dependencies; already reused as a child of root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_area_formula-a1.local_lipschitz_area-a1, whose accepted child disjoint_lipschitz_pieces consumes it). Its frozen Lean type, title and statement are copied byte-for-byte from that node, so the runtime maps this key onto the accepted checkpoint by Lean name and provisions no new worker; “parent step 1” in its title refers to root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.locally_lipschitz_image-a1. It replaces the earlier proposal to reuse lpf_lipschitz_localization, which the runtime rejected as reserved by an active node of another branch. The proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim. Use in lpf_chart_chain_rule: step 4 (covering the open set Φ⁻¹(U) ⊇ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) by countably many open sets on which f∘Φ is Lipschitz before applying Rademacher's theorem), consumed by the new child ae_diff_comp (Submission.lpf_ccr_ae_differentiableAt_comp), step 3.

Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). `LocallyLipschitzOn U f` means: for every x ∈ U there are K ∈ ℝ≥0 and a set t ∈ 𝓝[U] x (a neighbourhood of x within U) such that f is K-Lipschitz on t (`LipschitzOnWith K f t`: edist (f y) (f z) ≤ K · edist y z for all y, z ∈ t). Being K-Lipschitz on a set passes to its subsets (`LipschitzOnWith.mono`), and every map is 0-Lipschitz on ∅ (`lipschitzOnWith_empty`).

1. (Local open pieces.) Fix x ∈ U and choose K_x ∈ ℝ≥0 and t_x ∈ 𝓝[U] x with f K_x-Lipschitz on t_x. A set belongs to 𝓝[U] x iff it contains O ∩ U for some open O ∋ x (Mathlib `mem_nhdsWithin`). So there is an open O_x ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ O_x and O_x ∩ U ⊆ t_x, and f is K_x-Lipschitz on O_x ∩ U by monotonicity. (For x ∉ U put O_x := ∅ and K_x := 0, so x ↦ O_x is a total function. These values are never used: the Lindelöf step below only involves O_x for x ∈ U, and every point it returns lies in U.)

2. (Lindelöf.) ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so every subset of ℝ^P, in particular U, is Lindelöf (Mathlib instance `SecondCountableTopology.toHereditarilyLindelof`, lemma `HereditarilyLindelofSpace.isLindelof U`). For x ∈ U the open set O_x contains x, so O_x ∈ 𝓝 x. The neighbourhood form of the Lindelöf property (Mathlib `IsLindelof.elim_nhds_subcover`; equivalently, the open cover {O_x : x ∈ U} of U has a countable subcover) gives a countable set T ⊆ U with U ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ T} O_x.

3. (Case T = ∅.) Then U ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ ∅} O_x = ∅, so U = ∅. Take O_i := ∅ and K_i := 0 for every i ∈ ℕ. Each O_i is open, U = ∅ ⊆ ⋃_i O_i, and f is 0-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U = ∅.

4. (Case T ≠ ∅.) A nonempty countable set is the range of a sequence (Mathlib `Set.Countable.exists_eq_range`), so T = {g(i) : i ∈ ℕ} for some g : ℕ → ℝ^P. Put O_i := O_{g(i)} and K_i := K_{g(i)}. Since g(i) ∈ T ⊆ U, step 1 shows that O_i is open and f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U for every i.

5. (Cover.) Let x ∈ U. By step 2 there is y ∈ T with x ∈ O_y, and y = g(i) for some i ∈ ℕ, so x ∈ O_{g(i)} = O_i. Hence U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i. Together with step 4 (or step 3 when T = ∅) this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each x ∈ U choose K_x and an open O_x ∋ x with O_x ∩ U ⊆ t_x (mem_nhdsWithin), so f is K_x-Lipschitz on O_x ∩ U.
ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so some countable T ⊆ U has U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} O_x.
If T = ∅ then U = ∅, and O_i = ∅, K_i = 0 work.
Otherwise T = range g; put O_i := O_{g(i)} (open) and K_i := K_{g(i)}. Then f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U and U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i.

subproblems.title: Pulling Hⁿ-a.e. properties of M ∩ Φ(Ω) back to Lⁿ-a.e. parameters of an antilipschitz chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be (Borel) measurable, and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be (Borel) measurable with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, for some c > 0. Let p be any property of points of ℝ^P that holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ Φ(Ω) (∀ᵐ x for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))). Then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable (Lⁿ = volume), and p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (∀ᵐ w for Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (p : Eucl P → Prop), MeasurableSet Ω → Measurable Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ Φ '' Ω)), p x) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), p (Φ w)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure) on ℝ^P; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. For a measure μ and a set A, μ⌞A = μ.restrict A, and “q holds μ⌞A-a.e.” means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), q x. Write S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M).

This is steps 1–3 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule): Hⁿ-null exceptional sets in M ∩ Φ(Ω) pull back to Lⁿ-null sets of parameters, and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable, so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))-a.e. statements become Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))-a.e. statements.

0. (Null sets pull back.) Fix c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. The sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null) applied to (P, n, Φ, Ω, c) gives:
(N) for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.

1. (S is Lⁿ-null-measurable.) Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, there is a measurable set B ⊆ M with B = M Hⁿ-a.e. (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq); in particular Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (ae_eq_set). Because B ⊆ M,
S = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)):
if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∈ B, then w lies in the first set; if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∉ B, then Φ(w) ∈ M ∖ B and w lies in the second set; conversely both sets are contained in S because B ⊆ M and M ∖ B ⊆ M. The first set is measurable, since Ω and B are measurable sets and Φ is a measurable map. The second set has Lⁿ-measure 0 by (N) with Z := M ∖ B. The union of a measurable set and an Lⁿ-null set is Lⁿ-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.of_null, NullMeasurableSet.union). Hence S is Lⁿ-null-measurable; this is the first conjunct.

2. (The exceptional set in ℝ^P is Hⁿ-null.) Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ¬p(x)} ∩ (M ∩ Φ(Ω)). The hypothesis ∀ᵐ x ∂(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))), p x says exactly (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)))({x : ¬p(x)}) = 0 (ae_iff). For every measure μ and all sets s, t one has μ(t ∩ s) ≤ (μ⌞s)(t), with no measurability assumption on s or t (Mathlib Measure.le_restrict_apply). With s := M ∩ Φ(Ω) and t := {x : ¬p(x)} this gives Hⁿ(Z) ≤ 0, so Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

3. (The exceptional set of parameters is Lⁿ-null.) By (N), Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0. Let w ∈ S with ¬p(Φ(w)). Then w ∈ Ω, Φ(w) ∈ M, Φ(w) ∈ Φ(Ω) because w ∈ Ω, and ¬p(Φ(w)); hence Φ(w) ∈ Z and w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z). Thus {w : ¬(w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)))} = {w : w ∈ S ∧ ¬p(Φ(w))} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z), so this set is Lⁿ-null by monotonicity (measure_mono_null), i.e. ∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)) (ae_iff).

4. (Conclusion.) Since S is Lⁿ-null-measurable (step 1), for every property q one has (∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), q(w)) ⟺ (∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → q(w)) (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'₀). Applying this with q(w) := p(Φ(w)) to step 3 gives ∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), p(Φ(w)), the second conjunct. ∎

(Remark: the null-measurability of S from step 1 is what makes step 4 valid; for a non-measurable S the measure Lⁿ⌞S need not be concentrated on S.)
proof_key_steps: chart_preimage_null: every Hⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝ^P has Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
Choose a measurable B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)) is measurable ∪ Lⁿ-null, hence Lⁿ-null-measurable.
Z := {¬p} ∩ (M ∩ Φ(Ω)) satisfies Hⁿ(Z) ≤ (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)))({¬p}) = 0 (Measure.le_restrict_apply).
{w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) : ¬p(Φ w)} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) is Lⁿ-null, and ae_restrict_iff'₀ (using null-measurability) turns this into the restricted a.e. statement.

subproblems.title: Rademacher for f∘Φ: a.e. differentiability of a locally Lipschitz map composed with a C¹ map
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be locally Lipschitz on U, and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be of class C¹. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ (Lⁿ = volume): if Φ(w) ∈ U, then f∘Φ is (Fréchet) differentiable at w.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P), IsOpen U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n)), Φ w ∈ U → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, an additive Haar measure on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ. “f is locally Lipschitz on U” (Mathlib LocallyLipschitzOn U f) means: every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood t within U (t ∈ 𝓝[U] x) on which f is K-Lipschitz for some K ≥ 0. Write u := f∘Φ and O := Φ⁻¹(U).

This is step 4 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule): u is locally Lipschitz on the open set O, so covering O by countably many open sets on which u is Lipschitz and applying Rademacher's theorem to Lipschitz extensions shows that u is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. point of O.

1. (O is open.) Φ is C¹, hence continuous, and U is open, so O = Φ⁻¹(U) is open.

2. (u is locally Lipschitz on O.) Let w ∈ O and x := Φ(w) ∈ U.
- Since f is locally Lipschitz on U, there are K₁ ≥ 0 and t₁ ∈ 𝓝[U] x such that f is K₁-Lipschitz on t₁. As U is open and x ∈ U, 𝓝[U] x = 𝓝 x (IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq), so t₁ is a neighbourhood of x.
- A C¹ map is locally Lipschitz (Mathlib ContDiff.locallyLipschitz), so there are K₂ ≥ 0 and a neighbourhood t₂ of w such that Φ is K₂-Lipschitz on t₂.
- By continuity of Φ at w, Φ⁻¹(t₁) is a neighbourhood of w, hence so is t := t₂ ∩ Φ⁻¹(t₁); in particular t ∈ 𝓝[O] w.
- Φ is K₂-Lipschitz on t and maps t into t₁, where f is K₁-Lipschitz; hence u = f∘Φ is K₁K₂-Lipschitz on t (LipschitzOnWith.comp).
So u is locally Lipschitz on O.

3. (Countable Lipschitz cover.) The sibling lemma countable_lipschitz_cover (Submission.lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover) applied with (P, Q, U, f) := (n, Q, O, u) gives open sets O_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and constants K_i ≥ 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that O ⊆ ⋃_i O_i and u is K_i-Lipschitz on s_i := O_i ∩ O for every i. Each s_i is open, as the intersection of the open sets O_i and O (step 1).

4. (Rademacher on each piece.) Fix i ∈ ℕ. Since u is K_i-Lipschitz on s_i and ℝ^Q is finite-dimensional, there is a Lipschitz map v_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q with v_i = u on s_i (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension; alternatively the componentwise McShane extension x ↦ inf_{y∈s_i}(u^l(y) + K_i|x − y|) of Simon Ch. 2, 1.2). By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt for the additive Haar measure Lⁿ; SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt), v_i is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ. Let w ∈ s_i be such a point. Since s_i is open, it is a neighbourhood of w on which u = v_i, so u is differentiable at w with the same derivative as v_i (DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence E_i := {w ∈ s_i : u is not differentiable at w} is Lⁿ-null. (Mathlib packages this step as LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem, which gives differentiability of u within s_i at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ s_i, followed by DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt, valid because s_i ∈ 𝓝 w for w ∈ s_i.)

5. (Conclusion.) E := ⋃_{i∈ℕ} E_i is Lⁿ-null as a countable union of null sets (ae_all_iff). Let w ∉ E with Φ(w) ∈ U. Then w ∈ O ⊆ ⋃_i O_i, so w ∈ O_i for some i, hence w ∈ s_i; since w ∉ E_i, u = f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Hence for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ, Φ(w) ∈ U implies that f∘Φ is differentiable at w. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ⁻¹(U) is open, and f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on it: compose a Lipschitz neighbourhood of f at Φ(w) (U open, so 𝓝[U] = 𝓝) with a Lipschitz neighbourhood of the C¹ map Φ at w.
countable_lipschitz_cover: open O_i with Φ⁻¹(U) ⊆ ⋃ O_i and f∘Φ K_i-Lipschitz on the open sets s_i := O_i ∩ Φ⁻¹(U).

Rademacher on each s_i (Lipschitz extension v_i and LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, packaged as LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem): f∘Φ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. point of the open set s_i.
Countable union over i ∈ ℕ (ae_all_iff); every w with Φ(w) ∈ U lies in some s_i.

subproblems.title: Directional derivative of a Lipschitz map along DΦ(w)s equals D(f∘Φ)(w)s (Simon Ch. 2, 4.7/4.10)
subproblems.statement: Let n, P, Q ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose f is K-Lipschitz (K ≥ 0) on some neighbourhood V of Φ(w), Φ is differentiable at w, and f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n P Q : ℕ) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (w : Eucl n), (∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (Φ w), LipschitzOnWith K f V) → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w → ∀ s : Eucl n, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) := fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w; “f is K-Lipschitz on V” means |f(y) − f(z)| ≤ K|y − z| for all y, z ∈ V; o(t) denotes a function of t ∈ ℝ that is little-o of t as t → 0.

This is the fact (DD) used in step 5 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule; Simon Ch. 2, 4.7 and 4.10): for small |t| both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w + ts)| = o(t), while f(Φ(w + ts)) = f(Φ(w)) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t).

Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ and put x := Φ(w), v := DΦ(w)s, b := D(f∘Φ)(w)s, g₁(t) := f(x + t v), g₂(t) := f(Φ(w + t s)) and h := g₁ − g₂ (t ∈ ℝ).

1. (Derivatives along the line.) The affine line ℓ(t) := w + t s satisfies ℓ(0) = w and has derivative s at t = 0. Since Φ is differentiable at w = ℓ(0), the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) shows that t ↦ Φ(w + t s) has derivative DΦ(w)s = v at t = 0. Since f∘Φ is differentiable at w, the chain rule likewise shows that g₂ = (f∘Φ)∘ℓ has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s = b at t = 0.

2. (First-order expansion of Φ along the line.) By step 1 and the little-o characterization of derivatives (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO), using Φ(w + 0·s) = x: Φ(w + t s) − x − t v = o(t) as t → 0.

3. (Both points eventually lie in V.) As t → 0, x + t v → x (continuity of t ↦ x + t v) and Φ(w + t s) → Φ(w) = x (the map t ↦ Φ(w + t s) is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0). Since V is a neighbourhood of x, there is a neighbourhood of t = 0 on which x + t v ∈ V and Φ(w + t s) ∈ V. For such t, because f is K-Lipschitz on V,
|h(t)| = |f(x + t v) − f(Φ(w + t s))| ≤ K|x + t v − Φ(w + t s)| = K|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|.

4. (h has derivative 0 at 0.) By step 3, h(t) = O(|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|) as t → 0, and by step 2 the latter is o(t); hence h(t) = o(t) (Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans_isLittleO). Moreover h(0) = f(x) − f(Φ(w)) = 0. So h(t) − h(0) − t·0 = o(t), i.e. h has derivative 0 at t = 0 (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO).

5. (Conclusion.) g₁ = g₂ + h pointwise, since g₂(t) + (g₁(t) − g₂(t)) = g₁(t). By steps 1 and 4 and the sum rule (HasDerivAt.add), g₁ has derivative b + 0 = b at t = 0, that is, HasDerivAt (fun t => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Chain rule along ℓ(t) = w + ts: t ↦ Φ(w + ts) has derivative DΦ(w)s and g₂(t) = f(Φ(w + ts)) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0.
Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − t·DΦ(w)s = o(t).
For t near 0 both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |g₁(t) − g₂(t)| ≤ K|Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − t·DΦ(w)s| = o(t).
h = g₁ − g₂ has h(0) = 0 and derivative 0 at 0, so g₁ = g₂ + h has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at 0.
